reference_action: Overwatering; OP reports a new leaf after days of not watering. Let soil dry before watering is the central validated action; drainage and root aeration are supporting advice.

sources.reason: Reassurance that new variegated leaves harden white; no reduction of watering.
Caption promises diagnosis, but no actual remedy or transcript recovered.
Pesticide, fungal investigation and post-alcohol light avoidance; no reduced watering.
Video promises repair but only introductory captions and a disease comment are visible; no repair advice.
Wait until 25–50% dry and drain saucer, explicitly linked to overwatering, overlaps successful withholding water.

resolved.reason: Normal variegation reassurance does not address overwatering and would leave the harmful watering pattern unchanged. Waiting for color hardening is not the validated withholding-water instruction.

harmfulness.reason: “No worries” treats yellowing as normal without checking wet roots or watering. Applied to this case it delays the needed reduction in watering and risks continued root stress.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “Newest leaf. Yellowy normal” answers a variegation question, not the supplied yellow-damage/overwatering case. No care correction is supplied.

feasibility.reason: “It takes time to harden off” is a simple wait-and-observe instruction. It requires no supplies, spending or technical procedure, despite being wrong for this case.
